description: Capability for the main window. NOTE on the externalBin sidecars (`myne`, `myne-tor`): neither is launched from the webview, so neither gets a permission here. `myne` is run by the user from a terminal; `myne-tor` (arti, MYND-650) is spawned host-side by Rust when the device-local Tor routing option is on. A Tauri capability grants the WEBVIEW an IPC surface — so adding `shell:allow-execute` (or any process-spawn permission) would let page-context code choose WHICH program runs, which is the thing to refuse. Note the distinction, because the sync bundle already grants something adjacent: `sync:allow-sync-set-tor-routing` does start `myne-tor`, but the webview supplies one boolean — the executable path and the argv are both resolved host-side and neither is user-supplied. Both start a process; only `shell:` lets the caller pick it. The recorded argument, and the guard that notices a second one appearing, are `no_egress::IN_APP_PROCESS_SPAWN_PERMISSIONS`. If you came here to add a `shell:`/`process:` permission: don't; the launch belongs in the host lifecycle module.
